item.title: Chiefs nose tackle Khyiris Tonga is playing almost as much offense as Travis Hunter
item.description: Jaguars cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter has been much-hyped for his status as a two-way player, first as a Heisman Trophy winner at Colorado and now in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter has been much-hyped for his status as a two-way player, first as a Heisman Trophy winner at Colorado and now in the NFL. But there's another two-way player in the NFL this season who hasn't received as much hype: Chiefs nose tackle and fullback Khyiris Tonga.

Like Hunter, Tonga has started every game on defense this season. Like Hunter, Tonga has played only limited offensive snaps this season. Tonga has two carries; Hunter has two catches. Both have picked up one first down.

Hunter plays a little bit more on offense, but not much more: Hunter has played 6.8 percent of the Jaguars' offensive snaps, while Tonga has played 4.2 percent of the Chiefs' offensive snaps.

The Jaguars have said Hunter is capable of being a full-time player at both wide receiver and cornerback, while the Chiefs consider Tonga only a situational short-yardage fullback in addition to his duties as a starter on the defensive line. But as far as their usage this season, both players are comparable.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, himself a former defensive player who occasionally lined up on offense as well, started using Tonga as a blocking fullback last season, when Tonga played 14 snaps on offense in New England. This year, Tonga signed a three-year, $21 million free agent contract with the Chiefs, and the Chiefs have increased his role on offense, including not just blocking but also running the ball.

Tonga said on the Chiefs’ YouTube channel that it was a thrill the first time he went into the offensive huddle with quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker.

"It was super cool," Tonga said. "Being in the offensive huddle is amazing, especially having the players we have, to share the huddle with them. The only thing in my mind was, Don't mess it up. I just went out there to have fun. It makes it easy blocking for a guy like K9."

Tonga even ran a route on a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass to Jalen Royals in Week 2, and Tonga said he was prepared to catch it if Mahomes threw to him but was a little relieved when Mahomes looked past him and threw to Royals.

"I was just making sure I didn't drop it. Look it in if it came to me. It went past me, so it was OK," Tonga said.

Could Tonga do anything else in Andy Reid's offense? He said he'd even be up for throwing the ball on a trick play if that gets called.

"Having a guy like 15, I hope they don't make me throw the ball, but if we have to I'm ready," Tonga said.

Tonga, who has also played 19 snaps on special teams this season, is willing to do whatever he has to do to help his team win.

item.title: Report: Eagles don't plan to place Jalen Hurts on Injured Reserve
item.description: The Eagles are reportedly not putting starting quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR even though he's out with a blood clot.
item.content:encoded:
Report: Eagles don't plan to place Jalen Hurts on Injured Reserve originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Eagles do not plan to place Jalen Hurts on Injured Reserve, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Saturday morning.

The 28-year-old Hurts, who is out for at least the Eagles’ game Sunday after being diagnosed with a blood clot, would have to miss a minimum of four games if he went on IR. That would have sidelined him at least until the Eagles’ first game after their bye week, Nov. 22 at the Linc vs. the Steelers.

By keeping him on the 53-man roster, the Eagles give themselves the flexibility to bring Hurts back before then if he’s medically cleared. 

The Eagles have not provided any timetable on Hurts’ possible return to action and with a condition like this there is no way to predict how long he could be sidelined.

After the Panthers, the Eagles face the Cowboys on a Monday night at the Linc and then they’re at Washington on a Sunday night and home vs. the Giants.

Hurts, the MVP of Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans in 2024, has only missed four games because of injury since becoming the Eagles’ full-time starter in 2021. He missed the Jets game in 2021 with an ankle injury, he missed two games in 2022 with a shoulder injury and he missed a game in 2024 with a concussion.

Since 2021, when he became a full-time starter, Hurts has started started 83 games, 5th-most in the NFL behind Josh Allen (89), Jared Goff (87), Justin Herbert (85) and Patrick Mahomes (84).

Tanner McKee will make his third career start in place of Hurts Sunday against the Panthers. He’s thrown five touchdowns and one interception in his career.

Hurts in his first season in Sean Mannion’s offense has completed a career-low 57.8 percent of his passes, thrown for a career-low 187 yards per game and has a career-low 84.7 passer rating. He’s thrown eight touchdowns and three interceptions.

item.title: Titans CEO Burke Nihill: Our organization believes in coach Robert Saleh, GM Mike Borgonzi
item.description: The Titans have fired a head coach or GM each of the last four years, but they say they're going to be patient with their current coach and GM.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans are 0-5 in head coach Robert Saleh's first season, and 3-19 five games into General Manager Mike Borgonzi's second season. But Titans CEO Burke Nihill says the franchise believes the right leadership is in place.

"I personally feel a sense of stability," Nihill told ESPN on Friday. "I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football. The train is on the tracks. It just hasn't picked up momentum, but it will. I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster."

Those comments would mean more coming directly from Titans owner Amy Adams-Strunk, but the ESPN report says Nihill is empowered to speak for her. Nihill says the organization knows the fans are frustrated.

"The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we're sorry," Nihill said. "There's nobody in this building that doesn't feel . . . a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we've let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun. I think it starts on the field and the state of the franchise. We're 0-5, and that's not nearly good enough. It hasn't been for a while."

The Titans fired General Manager Jon Robinson during the 2022 season, fired head coach Mike Vrabel after the 2023 season, fired General Manager Ran Carthon after the 2024 season and fired head coach Brian Callahan during the 2025 season. All those firings haven't turned the franchise around. Now they're pledging patience with Borgonzi and Saleh.

item.title: Why Jordan Mailata means so much to Eagles young OL
item.description: As adversity continues to strike the Eagles, Jordan Mailata has been the unquestioned leader of a very young OL group.
item.content:encoded:
Why Jordan Mailata means so much to Eagles young OL originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jordan Mailata looked exhausted.

Not long after the Eagles lost an absolute heart-breaker to the Jaguars in London, Mailata stood in front of reporters in the visitor’s locker room of Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to answer questions after an awful finish to what Mailata called “a week from hell.”

And you understand why it was so rough on him. Lane Johnson abruptly retired, then Cam Jurgens got traded to the Ravens, all while Landon Dickerson has been on IR, and then the Eagles finished off the week with a last second-loss to the Jaguars. Now on a three-game losing streak, Mailata and the Birds were facing a 7 1/2-hour flight home before trying to pick up the pieces.

But in that moment, Mailata also showed some strength when asked how to get over a week like that.

“Watch the film and move on,” he said. “Just watch the film. Now we have a couple days before the next opponent and I’ll deal with it then. Reach out to my guys, see how they’re doing and then pull my socks up. Because we’ve got another game to play and these boys need me. That’s how I look at it.”

These boys need me.

The Eagles’ offensive line has been in a constant state of flux all season and Mailata has been their rock. His young teammates have been leaning on him.

“I just saw him dig deeper into his character,” said Jake Majors, who made his first-career start against the Jaguars at center. “Because there’s so much going on from his normal. And when you determine your normal, you find comfort. And clearly that was changing for all of us. 

“But what’s so good about him is he has unwavering leadership. He’s a servant leader. He’ll do anything for this group. So we called him our anchor last week and he’s going to be our anchor. Because he keeps us sound. When things are going bad, when things are going good, he keeps our composure where it needs to be. He’s our leader.”

Mailata’s big message to his young teammates has been about riding the waves of a season. There are going to be highs, there are going to be lows. It’s about staying the course.

There’s no doubt that the Eagles have been going through a ton of adversity and they’re really feeling it on the offensive line. Against the Jaguars, the Eagles had two players making their first-career starts and another making his second-career start. At one point, Mailata was the last man standing from the Week 1 starting line.

“We were really just saying it is what it is now,” right tackle Markel Bell said. “One thing we were saying is nobody is coming to save us. I know the type of person [Mailata] is, the type of character he got, he ain’t going to quit on us. He’s going to step up to the occasion.”

Bell is starting to settle into his role as the Eagles’ right tackle after Johnson abruptly retired. But he admitted there’s a lot of mental stress on a young player to not make mistakes. Mailata’s leadership has been crucial for him.

Bell played much better in Week 5 than he did in Week 4. And, in general, the Eagles’ backup offensive line did some good things against the Jaguars.

“I for sure wasn’t perfect, nobody was perfect in that game,” Bell said. “But it came down to the wire and people were doubting the young O-line, us, the young O linemen. People were doubting us, they were saying we probably won’t ever win a game with this O-line and it came down to a field goal. And that was one of the better defenses in the NFL. I feel like that speaks volumes on how resilient we are and how well we’re being led by Jordan.”

Before this season, Mailata was voted as one of seven team captains. One of those seven retired last week, leaving Mailata as the unquestioned leader of the Eagles’ offensive line room.

“I don’t think it’s a secret how good of a leader he is and a teammate he is,” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said. “That’s why the guys vote him a captain. That’s why he has a C on his chest. He’s been great, no matter what the circumstances [are], at being the same guy every day. Jordan’s unique in the sense of he’s always trying to help himself get better, but he’s always looking out for others as well in every aspect, whether that’s on the field or off the field. He’s got a good heart, and I think that’s why he does have the C on his chest.”

Mailata, 29, is in Year 9 of his NFL career. At this point in his incredible story, he takes his leadership duties seriously. It’s something that comes naturally but also something he really thinks about.

This week, Mailata made a concerted effort to bring up his energy level for the sake of his teammates. And they felt it.

“Jordan always has energy,” Willie Lampkin said. “That’s Jordan Mailata. He always brings the juice. We love that, we need that. He always is the one hyping us up and always getting us to where we need to be.

“I’m so appreciative of Jordan, man. Every day he’s been pushing all the young guys to continue to get better, continue to stay focused and continue to be one group. Jordan’s the leader our group. We all love him. I love him. I appreciate him so much.”

The Eagles were dealt even more adversity this week when we learned Jalen Hurts has a blood clot in his leg that will keep him out for at least this game.

When asked about his comment that last week was a week from hell, Mailata provided some comedic relief with some gallows humor.

“I think I was a little early,” Mailata said. “I might have jumped the gun on that.”

Mailata was obviously concerned for Hurts, the same was he was for Johnson and Jurgens and Dickerson. But he couldn’t spend too much time wallowing. He had a room to lead.

And that means everything to those guys.

“Dude, can’t beat it,” Majors said. “It’s obvious we’re going through a lot of adversity. But people like Jordan Mailata are what help you get through adversity. We have a lot of young guys on this team and to have someone like him to look up to is very special.”

item.title: Eagles vs. Panthers predictions for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season
item.description: Here are our predictions for Eagles-Panthers in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles vs. Panthers predictions for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Eagles (2-3) host the Panthers (2-2) on Sunday afternoon at Lincoln Financial Field.

Here are our predictions:

Reuben Frank (4-1)

I have absolutely no explanation for why I’m picking the Eagles. They’re missing most of their good players, the franchise seems like it’s in chaos, they haven’t scored a 2nd-half touchdown in a month, they’re down to their 4th-string running back, they’ll start their fifth offensive line in six weeks, their quarterback is out indefinitely with blood clots and a guy who was the 3rd-stringer two weeks ago is going to start Sunday against a pretty good Panthers team. So what’s my rationale? I don’t have one. What’s my logic? There is none. I just feel like sometimes when things look the worst you get surprised. So maybe the Eagles will shock the world Sunday and win a football game nobody expects them to win. Maybe Tanner McKee will play really well. Maybe the defense will shut down Bryce Young and Chuba Hubbard. Maybe the offense will score its first 3rd-quarter touchdown since the last day of the regular season last year. Maybe the team will rally around the chaos and find a way to win. Maybe not, but I’m going to choose to believe. 

Eagles 27, Panthers 23

Dave Zangaro (4-1)

Early in the week, I was leaning toward picking the Eagles in this game but then we found out that Jalen Hurts was out. And even though I’m intrigued to watch Tanner McKee play in this game, that was enough for me to flip my pick and go with the Panthers. But I think it’s going to be close and I think the Eagles really do have a shot to win this game. We just need to see more on offense with this group, especially in the second half. Over the last three games, their second half production has been abysmal and they have scored just three points. With DeVonta Smith back, the Eagles should be better on offense but they’re still missing some big pieces.

The Eagles’ defense will get Jonathan Greenard back for this game but is now without Jalyx Hunt. Still, the Eagles’ defense has been very good recently and is continuing to get better. They will do enough for the Eagles to win this game but I just don’t have enough faith in the offense to come through.

Panthers 23, Eagles 21

Barrett Brooks (4-1)

At 2-3, most would think this season is over. I know everyone is ready to secure a high draft pick and punt on the season. I’m not at that point right now — but I don’t think we are ready to go to the Super Bowl. One thing I do know is that we can’t afford to lose anyone else. Losing QB1 is definitely the last straw. The camel’s back has already been broken. My Birds can’t go any lower. So, I think there is a chance that things move in a better direction. Hopefully Landon Dickerson is back in the lineup. Landon at 80% is better than any backup we can start at left guard. C Drew Kendall looks like he may be able to start this Sunday. If he is not ready, I’m totally confident C/G Willie Lampkin can start and probably play better than any center that has played this year. DeVonta Smith is back for starting QB Tanner McKee this Sunday. That could be a huge boost for McKee, having two starters back in the lineup.

The defense will have to save the day. They have shown massive improvements at all three levels. Having DT Jalen Carter finally playing at an elite level and DE Jonathan Greenard back gives the defense a chance to go QB Bryce Young hunting. The secondary will have to play great to stop both WR Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker. I’m confident that the defense will keep us in the game and the offense finally shows up on Sunday.

Eagles 26, Panthers 24

Mike Mulhern (4-1)

No team coming back from overseas facing an opponent off the bye has ever won. Add in Jalen Hurts getting a blood clot and being ruled out, and it’s hard to be optimistic about this one.

Bryce Young has been lighting it up through the air. Tetairoa McMillan and the returning Jalen Coker offer a potent punch of big bodies on the outside. Chuba Hubbard has been a weapon out of the backfield. Yet I’m just not totally sold on the Panthers. With Jonathan Greenard back and Jalen Carter playing like the $152 million man the Eagles paid him to be, Vic Fangio’s group should be able to get after the quarterback and rattle him. The question becomes if the offense can do enough to steal a win.

The past few weeks have been a parade of three-and-outs that left the defense gassed at the end of games. The return of DeVonta Smith should open things up, despite the Birds being down to their fourth-string running back in Dameon Pierce and once-third-string quarterback, Tanner McKee. A loss sends them spiraling further into the abyss. A win could start to save what so far has been the season from hell. The Eagles always seem to show up for Nick Sirianni, and they do it again on Sunday.

Eagles 23, Panthers 20

Ashlyn Sullivan (5-0)

I don’t think this Eagles team are as bad as they have looked the past couple of weeks. Philadelphia is sitting at one game under .500 with an un-competitive NFC East and a couple close games that could have resulted in wins if a few plays go a different direction. I am not going to say they have been perfect, but the injuries the Eagles have dealt with are unbelievable, that will turn in time. The offense is getting back DeVonta Smith and possibly Landon Dickerson and sounds like defensive end Jonathan Greenard will be playing Sunday as well. I think Tanner McKee is going to compliment what Sean Mannion is trying to do on offense and will be more aggressive with passing attempts than what we have seen from Jalen Hurts the past couple of weeks. The Carolina Panthers are better than I expected, but I think Smith and Dallas Goedert are going to expose their young, weak secondary. Eagles win a close football game and snap a three-game losing streak.

Eagles 22, Panthers 17

Ryan Fowler (5-0)

As they have the last three weeks, everyone is ready to count out the Eagles this week with injuries in abundance. Jalen Hurts is out, as is Saquon Barkley, the line is a shell of itself, the offense has no continuity or identity… All of those are good reasons to side with an improving Carolina group this week, but not me. I’m bullish on Tanner McKee and what he represents at the quarterback position. He’s a throwback pocket passer with a bit of a gunslinger mentality and I think that works to the Eagles’ advantage against a Panthers secondary littered with first and second year players. McKee also has nothing to lose — he’s playing to prove to himself he can start in the NFL, to the Eagles, and to a group of other teams that have already shifted their focus to 2027 and beyond. On film, there’s been holes in the ground game that have not been hit and players in space that Hurts’ has had hesitancy in letting it rip to the last few weeks. It’s not to say McKee will be perfect, he won’t, but I don’t think he’ll be shy in throwing the football downfield to what looks to be a WR core with DeVonta Smith back in the fold.

Defensively, adjustments on the fly will be huge this week. Bryce Young has taken a huge step in adjusting to what defenses are throwing at him pre-snap, and mixing up pressure/coverage looks will remain paramount. They have talent on offense, but I’ll take Quinyon Mitchell over Tetairoa McMillan every day of the week and force others on Carolina’s offense to beat you on Sunday. The Panthers absolutely have enough talent — and have executed at a high enough level — to win in Philadelphia this week, but let’s not forget this is the same team that allowed 59 points to the Bears to open the year and lost to the Cleveland Browns on the road just a few weeks ago. 

Give me the Eagles here with their backs against the wall behind a defense that has played its tail off the past two weeks.

Eagles 20, Panthers 17

item.title: Roob's Eagles Observations: What makes Tanner McKee unique
item.description: A rare late-round quarterback, thoughts on Landon Dickerson’s future and recalling Rhett Hall’s blood clot scare three decades ago.
item.content:encoded:
Roob's Eagles Observations: What makes Tanner McKee unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Roob’s 10 Random Eagles Observations picks up the pieces after a challenging few weeks in Eagles World. Just think, in the span of 18 days, the Eagles got blown out by the Bears, blew a 10-point 4th-quarter lead against the Rams, flew back and forth to London, lost a game to the Jaguars after taking the lead with eight seconds left, dealt with Lane Johnson retiring, Cam Jurgens getting traded, Saquon Barkley getting hurt (among others) and finally learned of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots. 

“And it’s only Week 6,” Jordan Mailata bellowed at his locker on Thursday.

Who knows what the rest of the season will bring, but all I know is we’ll have 10 Obs every week.

WHAT ABOUT TANNER? While we all hope for a speedy recovery for Jalen Hurts and hope to see him back on the field as soon as possible, for now Tanner McKee is the Eagles’ quarterback, and it’s rare for a quarterback drafted as late as McKee to start regular-season NFL games. In their long 94-year history, the Eagles have had only one other quarterback drafted in the sixth or seventh round start a game. Koy Detmer, a 7th-round pick in 1997, went 3-5 in eight starts from 1998 through 2004. McKee, a 6th-round pick in 2023, is 1-1 in two starts going into the Panthers game Sunday at the Linc. The only other NFL quarterback drafted in the sixth or seventh round who’s started a game this year is Brock Purdy, the 49ers’ 7th-round pick in 2022. Purdy, Tom Brady and Matt Hasselbeck are the only quarterbacks drafted in the sixth round or later to win a playoff game in the last 20 years. Guys like Tyrod Taylor and Gardner Minshew have had sporadic success, but the last 6th– or 7th-round QB other than Brady and Purdy to win 10 games in a season was Ryan Fitzpatrick with the Jets in 2015 and before that Matt Cassel with the Patriots in 2010. Of 165 quarterbacks in NFL history drafted in the sixth or seventh round to throw at least 50 passes, McKee’s 95.7 passer rating is 3rd-highest, not surprisingly behind Purdy (105.4) and Brady (97.2). He’s thrown five TDs in his brief career and just one interception. McKee is smart, accurate and confident, gets rid of the ball quickly, knows the offense and is respected by his teammates. He’s not Jalen, but I expect him to be fine as long as he’s in there. Which hopefully isn’t too long. 

LANDON’S FUTURE: I keep going back to this: If the Eagles were totally willing to trade Cam Jurgens, why wouldn’t they be totally willing to trade Landon Dickerson as well? If the offer is right? I think Howie would do it, for all the same reasons – freeing up a huge amount of future cash, moving on from a late-20s interior lineman who’s best days are likely behind him and adding to the growing draft pick stockpile. One difference is that the Eagles believed they already had an heir apparent to Jurgens in Drew Kendall, and I’m not sure they feel the same way about any of their other young interior linemen – Jake Majors, Willie Lampkin or Micah Morris. But they can figure out left guard. I think we’re seeing the first couple steps on what’s going to be an almost total o-line overhaul. Lane Johnson, Cam Jurgens and Dickerson made a combined 11 Pro Bowls and they could all be gone fairly soon. And don’t forget, Tyler Steen is unsigned beyond this year and with his level of play dropping off from last year they could be replacing everybody on the o-line other than Jordan Mailata. Which is crazy. Howie has drafted well on the o-line over the years with a couple notable exceptions that you know all too well, and he may need to repeat that success over the next year or two.

ON RHETT HALL AND BLOOD CLOTS: Do you guys remember Rhett Hall? He was a defensive tackle that Ray Rhodes brought over to Philly with him in 1995 after Hall played for Rhodes on the 1994 Super Bowl-champion 49ers. It was just after training camp in August of 1995 that Eagles defensive line coach Mike Trgovac noticed that Hall didn’t look well. Hall complained that his resting pulse was racing at twice its normal rate, and trainer Otho Davis came over and checked him out and immediately knew something serious was happening. Hall was rushed to Thomas Jefferson Hospital, where he was diagnosed with multiple blood clots that had reached his lungs. Quick action by Trgo and Otho probably saved Hall’s life. He was treated with blood thinners and missed three months of the season before finally getting cleared in late November and returning for two games before suffering a season-ending knee injury that knocked him out of the playoffs. Hall played three more seasons with the Eagles without any complications from the clots. “When you’re diagnosed with something like that, it helps you put football in perspective,” Hall said in an interview on the Eagles’ web site in 2010. “My first and foremost thought was getting healthy. It was just within a matter of weeks I felt like I’m going to be fine and I’m going to play again. It’s just a matter of how long it’s going to take to get back out there.” Was a scary time and quite a scare for Hall, and who knows how comparable his situation was with Hurts currently but certainly encouraging that as grave as Hall’s condition was he was able to return later that year and play three more seasons with no issues. It was lingering knee issues that ultimately ended Hall’s career after the 1998 season.

HE DID WHAT AT 35 YEARS OLD???: Did you ever stop and consider how remarkable Irving Fryar’s 1997 season was?  Fryar was 35 when he caught 86 passes for 1,316 yards, with was 300 more yards than anybody had ever had at that age and remains the most ever by a player 35 or older. Fryar also had 1,195 yards in 1996 at 34 years old and is one of only three players with multiple seasons of 1,150 yards after his 34th birthday. The others are Hall of Famers Cris Carter and Jerry Rice. Fryar’s 3,869 yards after his 34th birthday are 5th-most in NFL history. And one more amazing Irving Fryar stat: Only two other Eagles have had 85 catches and 1,300 yards in their 20s – A.J. Brown and Jeremy Maclin. Fryar did it when he was 35. And the most receiving yards in a season by an Eagles WR 35 and over other than Fryar? Hall of Famer James Lofton with 167 in 1993 at 37 years old. 

WHAT’S WRONG WITH THIS PICTURE? The Eagles have started 24 drives on their own 30-yard-line and in and scored three touchdowns on those 24 drives. The other 21 drives have ended like this: 13 punts, four interceptions, one fumble and three downs. The only team to score fewer touchdowns when starting drives at their own 30 and in is the Broncos, who have just one. For the sake of comparison, the Rams, Panthers, Bills and Cowboys have all scored nine times on drives of 70 yards or more. The league average is 20.1 percent. The Eagles are at 12.5 percent.

JALEN HURTS STAT OF THE DAY: The Jaguars game was Jalen Hurts’ 42ndin 87 career starts with at least one touchdown and no interceptions. The only quarterbacks with more games with a TD pass and no INTs through 87 career starts are Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes with 44 each. Of 22 Hall of Fame quarterbacks, Steve Young had the most such games with 34.

DARIUS COOPER’S RARE PRODUCTION: Darius Cooper is the first undrafted NFL wide receiver 24 or younger with four touchdowns through five games in 41 years. In 1985, Dennis McKinnon of the Bears, who was also 24, had six touchdowns through Week 5 as the Bears made their way to a Super Bowl championship. Only five other undrafted WRs since 1970 have had four TDs the first five of a season before their 25th birthday: Willie Frazier of the Oilers in 1965, Dan Reeves of the Cowboys in 1968, Steve Watson of the Broncos in 1981 and Bobby Johnson of the Giants in 1984.

HOW BAD HAVE THEY BEEN AFTER HALFTIME? Here are five mind-blowing stats illustrating how bad the Eagles have been in the second half this year:

  • The Eagles have an NFL-low 21 offensive plays of 10 yards or more after halftime.
  • The Eagles have recorded just 24 first downs after halftime, 11 fewer than next-worst, the Dolphins with 35. They’re last in passing first downs in the second half with 16 – four fewer than the Chiefs and Dolphins – and 31st in rushing first downs with eight, somehow two more than the Packers.
  • The Eagles are converting just 29.7 percent on third down in the second half, which is 30th in the league, ahead of the Steelers (26.7 percent) and Ravens (25.9 percent). 
  • The Eagles are gaining an average of 3.5 yards per play in the second half, nearly a yard worse than any other team. The Vikings are 31st at 4.3 yards per play in the second half. 
  • The Eagles have scored on just five of 29 2nd-half drives, worst in the league. The Titans are next-worst with six scores after halftime. They have two touchdowns in the second half, half as many as the Colts and Titans. The league average is teams scoring on 40 percent of 2nd-half drives. The Eagles are scoring on a league-worst 17 percent with nobody else under 27 percent. The league average is scoring touchdowns on 25 percent of drives. The Eagles are at an NFL-worst 7 percent, with nobody else under 17 percent.  

THE MISERABLE SACK STATS: The Eagles’ six sacks match their fewest through five games since 1993, when they had five. They also had six after five weeks in 1997. Their edge rushers have combined for just two sacks, both by Nolan Smith. Eagles starting edge rushers with no sacks through five games since sacks became an official stat in 1982: Clyde Simmons (1990), Mike Mamula (1997), Greg Jefferson (1999), Ndukwe Kalu (2003), Trent Cole (2013), Derek Barnett (2021), Jalyx Hunt (2025), Jalyx Hunt (2026). 

ALAS POOR JORRICK: Britain Covey had a 41-yard punt return vs. the Rams and a 42-yard kick return vs. the Jaguars. The last Eagle with punt and kick returns of at least 40 yards in the same season was Jorrick Calvin, who had a 44-yard punt return against the Falcons in Week 6 and a 41-yard kick return against the Titans a week later. The 44-yarder was the sixth punt return of Calvin’s career and the 41-yarder was the seventh kick return of his career. Calvin played 12 games with the Eagles in 2010, the only NFL games he ever played. Others who have pulled off the 40-yard return double since 1941, as far back as return stats go: Steve Van Buren in 1944, Bosh Pritchard and Buren in 1946, Pritchard in 1948, Clyde Scott in 1949, Don Stevens in 1952, Al Pollard in 1953, Billy Wells in 1958, Art Powell in 1959, Timmy Brown in 1961 and 1964, Irv Cross in 1965, Aaron Martin in 1966, Alvin Haymond in 1968, Billy Walik in 1971, Larry Marshall in 1977, Wally Henry in 1981, Vai Sikahema in 1992, Mark Seay in 1996, Brian Mitchell in 2000, 2001 and 2002 and Brian Westbrook in 2003.

item.title: Eagles' Jonathan Greenard hungry as he makes his return in frustrating season
item.description: It has been a frustrating season for Jonathan Greenard but he's hungry as he makes his return on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles' Jonathan Greenard hungry as he makes his return in frustrating season originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jonathan Greenard tries to have some perspective. He knows injuries are a part of football and he knows there are other players who have it much worse than him.

But it still hurts to miss game action.

“That’s the most frustrating part out of everything, that I still can’t play ball,” Greenard said on Friday. “I can’t be out on that field, that s— hurts my soul and it eats me up. But I know that day is soon going to come. I see the light at the end of the tunnel and we’re going to turn this s— around.”

The light at the other end of the tunnel is real and Greenard will make his return from an ankle injury on Sunday against the Panthers. Greenard missed the game in London but does not have a game status for Week 6. He’s good to go.

The Eagles pulled off a draft-weekend trade for Greenard in April and then gave him a $98 million contract to become their top-of-the-rotation edge rusher. But nothing has gone to plan. Greenard suffered a pec strain in the team weight room just before training camp that kept him out all summer and for the first two weeks of the season.

And then, in his second game back, Greenard suffered an ankle injury that put him on the shelf again.

Greenard, 29, flew all the way to London last week and worked out before the Jaguars game before the decision was made that he was inactive.

“It’s tough,” Greenard said. “You can’t play the game you love, what they brought you here to do, can’t do your job at the highest level. But it comes with this. Injuries are a part of it and I didn’t ask for it. It just comes with it. 

“You just gotta be able to persevere through it, understand that you’re not the only one and other people have it much worse. Just try to find that victory every single day and seeing what the next day brings.”

The Eagles will definitely need Greenard this week because Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) has been ruled out and A.J. Epenesa (back) is doubtful. That leaves Greenard, Nolan Smith and Arnold Ebiketie as the remaining edge rushers on the Eagles’ 53-man roster.

Greenard is a former Pro Bowler who had 24 1/2 sacks from 2023-2024. The Eagles were banking on that type of production in 2026 but Greenard has played just 37 defensive snaps so far this season.

On Friday, Greenard was asked if it’s fair to say Eagles fans haven’t seen his best yet.

“That’s absolutely fair,” Greenard said. “Fair to myself. I know what can do. I genuinely know what I can do. I know the impact I can have on this game. I still feel like I’m one of the best at my position. I like myself against anybody. It’s a matter of getting out there and showing it and putting it on tape. I know it’s there. I just gotta get out there. 

“It’s frustrating but I don’t let it get me down. I got my family at home to continue to keep me in good spirits and my friends, my teammates, my locker room. It’s a great locker room despite everything that’s going on. Everybody is still just pushing, understanding that nobody’s going to come save us. We’ve got to get ourselves out this hole. And we like that. We like the challenge.”

To Greenard’s point, he has flashed in limited time. Even though he has played just 37 defensive snaps this season, Greenard has four pressures. That’s a pressure rate of 15.4% on 26 rushes. 

His last pressure came in the third quarter against the Rams when he injured his ankle.

“S—, the play I got hurt, I almost had a strip sack,” Greenard said. “It’s there. Something’s gotta be coming. L after little L, eventually a dub is coming. I’m going to wait for that day to come, keep staying prayed up and continue to do what they ask me to do here and when I get out there, y’all know I’ll be ready.”

item.title: Eagles notebook: Time to see Carson Steele on offense?
item.description: In the latest Eagles notebook: Carson Steele's time on offense, lefty QBs and more.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles notebook: Time to see Carson Steele on offense? originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

As Carson Steele began to hear the the question about the Eagles’ running back room, he jumped in to help. The running back room is a little …

“A little banged up,” Steele said.

No kidding.

The Eagles will be without Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) this weekend when they host the Carolina Panthers. Those were the three running backs the Eagles went into the year with on their 53-man roster.

Last week, the Eagles started Shipley but then he injured his foot and left the game. That left them with Dameon Pierce and Steele, who began the year on the practice squad. So with Shipley now out and Barkley and Bigsby still out, the Eagles go into this game against the Panthers with Pierce and Steele as their top two options.

“It’s unfortunate but it’s a blessing to be on the field,” Steele said. “So it’s kind of a toss up. I’m just excited for an opportunity. That’s really all I can say. I hope my guys heal up, get back out on the field and I’m going to try to help them in any way possible.”

Last week, Steele played 20 special teams snaps but didn’t see the field on offense. That seems likely to change this weekend with yet another injury at the running back position.

“Not excited that guys are hurt,” Steele said, “but excited to possibly get an opportunity and just go from there.”

During the preseason, Steele was a star with 14 catches for 136 yards and 2 touchdowns coming out of the backfield. He also had 59 rushing yards on 21 carries. If he plays on offense Sunday, it’ll be his first time doing that since the 2024 season with the Chiefs.

Even though Barkley has been out, the All-Pro back has been really helpful to the other backs, especially because Barkley now has a different vantage point.

“He’ll point out a few things and at the beginning you’re just trying to get the play down and the protection and you’re not thinking of that until the very end,” Steele said. “Then you go back and look at the film and go, ‘Damn, he was right.’ He gets that bird’s-eye view so that really helps out.”

Second-half ineptitude

How bad have the Eagles been on offense in the second half during their three-game losing streak? You’ve got to see it to believe it.

The next lefty QB?

Because Jalen Hurts is out this week with a blood clot in his calf, Tanner McKee is the starter against the Panthers and fifth-round pick Cole Payton is the Eagles’ backup.

If Payton gets to throw a pass this year, he will become the first lefty quarterback to attempt a pass for the Eagles since Michael Vick in the 2013 season. On Friday, I asked Payton who his favorite all-time lefty quarterback is and his answer was Vick. That’s a pretty good one.

Vick is one of the best lefty QBs of all time. Some of the other names you’ll see mentioned in that conversation are Steve Young, Ken Stabler, Boomer Esiason and Mark Brunell.

The last lefty to throw a pass in an Eagles uniform was not Vick. It was actually running back Kenny Gainwell, who completed a 17-yard pass against the Cardinals in 2023.

The Eagles have had just five lefties throw a pass for them in a regular season game: Gainwell (1 attempt), Vick (1,300 attempts), Akers (1 attempt), Allie Sherman (135 attempts) and Ed Matesic (124 attempts) Sherman played in the 40s and Matesic played in the 30s. And the Eagles also had lefty Tim Tebow in the 2015 preseason but he didn’t make the 53-man roster that year.

More mobility for Jalen Carter

Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter was able to wear a smaller cast on his right wrist for Week 5 against the Jaguars and had his best game of the season with a couple strip sacks and another tackle for loss.

And there’s more good news coming about that cast.

“I think it’s going to be significantly smaller this week,” DC Vic Fangio said.

Carter has been dealing with this injury for a few weeks but has said eventually he won’t have to wear the cast anymore and will get full use of his hands back. That’s a huge deal for a defensive lineman. And on Sunday, we finally saw the player the Eagles need after making Carter the highest-paid DT in NFL history.

The Eagles need more consistency from Carter.

“I just think as he progresses as a player, understands what’s important from a technique standpoint and how to play, we’ll get more of that,” Fangio said. “But it’s not like he’s been not playing good since he’s been here. It’s just he obviously made a couple big plays the other night and hopefully that will continue and it’s hopefully his wrist (is) getting better.”

Still enjoying the job

Through five weeks the Eagles’ offense has been worse than anyone expected. While they’ve dealt with plenty of injuries, it’s still fair to expect them to have better than the second-worst offense in the NFL.

Going by yards, that’s where the Eagles are at just 262.2 yards per game — behind just the 0-5 Titans at 246.4.

But those struggles haven’t yet sucked the fun out of the job for first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, whose eyes lit up this week when asked about his adjustment to the position.

“I know we’re fighting tooth and nail every day to get the results that I know we can get, the results I know we want,” Mannion said. “The thing with the work part of it is it really is — that’s the part you love. You love coming in here every day, working your tail off with your staff, with your players, working as a unit to try to achieve the best result possible. I know we’re still fighting for what we want that to look like, but my enthusiasm, my enjoyment with that process has not waned in the slightest. It’s been a blast.

“There are new challenges every day, whether it be managing injuries or whether it be managing a practice plan or traveling overseas, how does that adjust our offensive meeting schedule? But that honestly is the enjoyable part. That’s why you love getting into coaching is you get to work with other great coaches, get to work with a phenomenal group of players that work their butts off, they’re coachable, they want to win, they want to get better.

“It’s a new challenge every day in this role, but it’s everything I hoped it would be and it’s been a blast. I am really confident that if we keep attacking each day with the right mindset, with a high level of enthusiasm, with a will to just get better bit by bit, day by day, we are going to get the results that we’re after.”

item.title: Golden Nuggets: What a sublime Saturday to trade for a pass-rusher
item.description: Your daily San Francisco 49ers news for Saturday, October 17th, 2026
item.content:encoded:
49ers injury updates: Kyle Juszczyk practices in full; 2 rookies miss
“Wide receiver Mike Evans didn’t practice for the second day in a row. This is likely how it’ll be with Evans this year. Even if he doesn’t practice, he’ll still suit up on game day.

Defensive tackle Gracen Halton missed a second straight day with a quad injury. That’s suboptimal, given the injuries at the position. The 49ers are as thin as you can be at the position. The silver lining is that James Thompson was listed as limited, although that’s not a 1-for-1 swap.

Rookie Romello Height was a new addition after practicing in full on Thursday. Height’s designation is an illness, so the hope is that he’s fine, with the game still 72 hours away.”

49ers’ John Lynch says he’s shopping before NFL trade deadline; Kittle asks about Khalil Mack (paywall)
“When asked on KNBR on Friday morning about the 49ers possibly trading for Mack, 35, Lynch said “a lot of people ask me that” before revealing Kittle posed the question Thursday.

“It’s usually Kittle because he asks about everything, which I love,” Lynch said….“I just like to chirp him and ask what he’s interested in and see if he’ll give me anything,” Kittle said. “So he didn’t really give me a lot yesterday. But me, (fullback Kyle Juszczyk), (left tackle) Trent (Williams), we’ll chirp him just to see if he’ll actually tell us anything. I think he tells Trent the most. Not me, though.”

Examining the 49ers’ early-season feat: Generating pressure without Nick Bosa (paywall)
“This year, Osa Odighizuwa already has 15 pressures after just five games while rookie Gracen Halton has seven. Odighizuwa’s 12.8 percent pass rush win rate ranks 12th at his position among those who have played five games. Halton’s is 9.6 percent, a rate Odighizuwa says ought to climb as Halton, a fourth-round pick, continues to improve his technique. Halton missed Thursday’s practice with a quadriceps injury.

“He’s very raw now,” Odighizuwa said. “So you’re just seeing nothing but upside when you’re watching him play. So it’s exciting stuff.”

John Lynch states 49ers trade discussions have ramped up ahead of deadline
“Just because the flow of the trade deadline is approaching, yes,” he said. “That’s our job to do that, to talk with our counterparts around the league. We receive calls, we make calls, just to see where the market is at.”

Raheem Morris, Klay Kubiak, Brock Purdy share updates ahead of 49ers-Commanders
“It was a lot of fun. I’ll give you a quick story. I remember people asking me, ‘How was it coaching [former NFL WR] Julio Jones?’ I said, ‘It’s easy. Good catch, Julio’ (laughter). No, all joking aside, you were able to take your defensive analysis and bring it to those guys while you were learning how to be a good offensive coach and the detail and everything that’s required. That goes into scoring touchdowns and staying on the field and manufacturing first downs. Being around Kyle that first year on offense, it was really the philosophy of what we’re trying to do on football games and how we’re going to go out there and attack people. I had so much fun being able to be over there with the likes of Kyle Shanahan, [Green Bay Packers head coach] Matt LaFleur, [Arizona Cardinals head coach] Mike LaFleur was on that staff, [Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator] Mike McDaniel. It was a bunch of really great coaches that were teaching me the backend. And in the frontend, you had all the guys on the front end like [assistant head coach/offensive line coach] Chris Foerster and those guys just teaching you what it was like in the run game and what the rules were and everything that was required to go out there and accomplish what we wanted to get accomplished. You can’t help but bring that back to defense when you had to go back over there. So, when I was able to go back and really formulate how I see the game, how I feel the game, how you want to make your players feel the game, that philosophy really helped me a lot to grow. I think everything from the beginning was really helpful for me when it came to offensive football.”

49ers Week 5 Trench Grades: The duality of it all (paywall)
“This week was defined by Gracen Halton dominating and Connor Colby getting dominated. After an encouraging start, Colby is officially a problem. Seattle attacked him, and what’s particularly cool is that I was able to really track that effectively.

Because I logged Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams as elite players (same for Demarcus Lawrence in the run game), we were able to identify that Seattle got Colby isolated against one of that elite pairing consistently. And he consistently lost. It’s one of the cooler reflections of tape to data thus far this season…..Keion White was a menace, and Romello Height is very clearly starting to cook, club and all. Mykel Williams also had a basic bull rush pressure that became White’s sack. It’s worth noting that Williams exclusively played on the edge this week. That’s easing him back into it. I would be stunned if that doesn’t change as the season goes.”

item.title: Titans CEO apologizes to fans for abysmal start — but still believes in Robert Saleh
item.description: The Titans are sorry for being sorry.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans are sorry for being sorry.

Tennessee, who has yet to win a game this season, is publicly acknowledging its failures so far while standing behind head coach Robert Saleh.

Titans CEO Burke Nihill apologized to fans Friday amid the team’s 0-5 start, telling ESPN that the franchise understands the frustration surrounding its continued struggles.

“I personally feel a sense of stability,” Nihill said in an interview with ESPN on Friday. “I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football. The train is on the tracks. It just hasn’t picked up momentum, but it will.”

Nihill added, “I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster.”

He continued, apologizing directly to the fans for the team’s winless 2026.

“The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we’re sorry,” Nihill told ESPN. “There’s nobody in this building that doesn’t feel … a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we’ve let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun.”

Saleh, who was the head coach of the Jets from 2021 to 2024, spent last season as the defensive coordinator of the 49ers prior to taking the Titans head coaching job this off-season.

“We’re going through a lot of adversity,” Saleh said. “But if we capture it the right way, we’re going to find a lot of growth, and when I tell you guys that the sun is going to shine on this organization eventually, it’s going to shine.”

This comes as the team is one of just three winless squads in the NFL with a -51 point differential, averaging under 12 points per game.

Quarterback Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in 2025, has faced increased pressure to produce amid the seemingly unstable environment.

One reporter asked him if he had gotten used to losing, to which Ward replied, “No, I’m not a loser. The record may say that we are right now. But at the end of the day, you have got to go through some stuff to try to get wins.”

Ward added, “We attack this each and every day, but for that, if you’re able to look at everyone in our locker room’s track record, we’ve all won games at a high level, and we’re looking forward to doing that in the long run.”

The Titans visit the Colts this Sunday in an attempt to avoid going 0-6.

Tennessee has gone 3-14 in each of its last two seasons, and they haven’t been to the playoffs since 2021.

item.title: Broncos star coming off commissioner’s exempt list — but still could be suspended
item.description: Cooper is facing a felony charge and three misdemeanors stemming from two incidents.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper was removed from the NFL’s commissioner exempt list on Friday.

Cooper, 28, has yet to be allowed to practice or play in games this season, but will now be available to play in Denver’s Week 7 matchup against the Cardinals.

Commissioner Roger Goodell placed Cooper on the exempt list on Aug. 30 after he was arrested twice in June on domestic violence charges.

Cooper is facing a felony charge and three misdemeanors stemming from the two incidents.

An arrest affidavit detailed that Cooper and his girlfriend were taken into police custody following an altercation at his apartment.

Cooper and his girlfriend were allegedly arguing over cheating allegations when the woman “grabbed Cooper’s phone from him and threw it across the room, then picked it up to go through it,” the report stated.

The pair then got into a physical altercation while Cooper took his phone back from her, according to the report.

According to the affidavit, Cooper “braced his neck against [her] neck to prevent her from getting his phone” and then bit and broke the phone.

In a social media post Friday, Cooper said that he has been “working to better myself” while awaiting trial.

“Playing in the NFL and representing the Denver Broncos is a privilege I do not take for granted,” Cooper wrote. “I’m grateful to ownership, my teammates, coaches and everyone in the organization for their support as well as Commissioner Goodell and the league for the opportunity to return.

“Over the last several months, I’ve spent a lot of time working to better myself. That work will continue. My focus is on being the best person, father, teammate and member of this community I can be. I will show that commitment through my actions every day.”

Cooper can still face additional discipline from the league at a later date, according to the NFL’s personal conduct policy.

item.title: Troy Aikman's role with the Dolphins hovers over his broadcasting future
item.description: Why would any network with options opt for someone who works for one of the NFL's teams?
item.content:encoded:
Troy Aikman's contract with ESPN expires after the 2026 season, which culminates in the four-letter network's first ever Super Bowl. Absent an extension, which Aikman currently doesn't expect, he'll become a broadcasting free agent.

His separate relationship with the Dolphins hovers over Aikman's future on TV.

Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, Aikman does not have a “formal and ongoing agreement” to serve as a consultant with the Dolphins. This means that he's working for the team on an at-will basis, and that he (or the team) can end the relationship at any time.

It could be in Aikman's best interests to end the relationship with the Dolphins now. If ESPN (or CBS or Prime Video) will be paying $20 million or more for its top NFL analyst gig, why would any of them hire someone who has both restrictions on his access and a cloud over his objectivity, thanks to having an employment relationship with one of its teams.

Last month, Aikman "called bullshit" on the idea that other broadcasters don't have conflicts of interest. That misses the point. Aikman is employed by the Dolphins. That relationship prevents him from entering team facilities or attending practices — and it creates avoidable complications when it comes to games involving the team that employs him.

When ESPN's Jason Kelce refers to the Eagles as "we," it's because he used to play for the team. (And ESPN is trying to get him to knock it off.) When Aikman talks about the Dolphins, "we" is technically accurate; he works for the team.

For networks with options, why would any network opt for someone who is employed by one of the teams? Beyond Tom Brady (who owns a piece of the Raiders and has an even more obvious conflict of interest, even if Fox doesn't care), none of the other candidates for the biggest jobs in NFL broadcasting bring such baggage with them.

As to Aikman, the right decision is obvious if he hopes to get another high-profile broadcasting job. He should end his relationship with the Dolphins as soon as possible.

item.title: Spencer Brown is good to go, but five Bills remain questionable for Sunday’s game against the Raiders
item.description: Five Bills carry questionable tags into Sunday, but Spencer Brown is cleared, and no one has been ruled out.
item.content:encoded:
The Buffalo Bills will enter the weekend with five players listed with injury designations – and none of them are named Spencer Brown The other good news is, no one has been ruled out for Sunday afternoon’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. 

Both D.J. Moore and Joshua Palmer are questionable after a limited day of practice on Friday. For Moore, it was the first practice he participated in all week, while Palmer has spent the entire week limited. Both wide receivers are dealing with shoulder injuries. Neither of them played in last week’s Monday night marathon game.  

Ed Oliver practiced for the first time in two weeks. It was limited, but it was practice. Now the Bills’ defensive tackle is listed as questionable with the knee injury that kept him out of Week 5. 

T.J. Sanders had an emergency appendectomy a couple of weeks ago. He got back to work quickly, missing just two games. But then he collected a shoulder injury last week in Los Angeles. He spent the first two practices of this week limited but was listed as a full participant on Friday. Despite the upgrade, the Bills listed him as questionable for game day.  

Then there’s Dee Alford. The only nickel cornerback on the roster missed a game and a half after injuring his ankle in Buffalo’s loss to the New England Patriots in Week 4. He was limited all week this week and is, of course, listed as questionable for Sunday.  

Last week the Bills signed Anthony Kendall from the practice squad to the active roster. Not an elevation, a signing. Not only didn’t they send Alford to Injured Reserve, the released Kendall on Monday (they signed him back to the practice squad on Tuesday after the third year corner cleared waivers). All those signs might have indicated they expected Alford to play this week, but now they maybe aren’t so sure – or they’re being coy.  

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

On the other sideline, the Raiders have ruled out three players and listed another as questionable.  

Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was ruled out after not being able to make any progress in concussion protocol and spending the entire week not practicing at all.  

Trey Zuhne III, the Raiders’ back up right tackle, is questionable with a knee injury after a week of limited practice. 

As for the other two names on the Raiders list of designations, both Carter Runyen and Dont’e Thonton, Jr are working their way back from Injured Reserve. They are both working through their 21-day practice window at this time.

item.title: Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave
item.description: The NFL's decision to reinstate Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt list carried with it a conspicuous omission.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's decision to reinstate Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt list carried with it a conspicuous omission.

Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave.

All three landed on paid leave on Sunday, August 30. Both Jacobs and Cooper are returning after six games. Arnold will continue to wait.

The distinction highlights the evolution of paid leave. Now, the NFL uses it as a way to pre-suspend a player with pay for the number of games he's likely to miss once officially suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy. The player receives credit once he's suspended without pay for the games missed while on paid leave.

As to Arnold, who faces a potential sentence of life in prison due to eight felonies arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping, it makes sense for the league to wait for the criminal case against him to be resolved. While the standard punishment for a case of domestic battery is six games, the claims against Arnold could trigger something longer — especially in light of the potential criminal penalties.

Frankly, the NFL may never have to convert Arnold's paid leave into an unpaid suspension. If he ends up behind bars for the practical balance of his career, the length of the suspension won't matter.

item.title: What To Watch For: Syracuse Orange
item.description: CAN THE LOUISVILLE DEFENSE AVOID A LETDOWN If you have had the opportunity to read my film reviews this week, you know that your eyes didn’t deceive you when it comes to the defensive performance last weekend. Louisville made a legit change in the defensive scheme when they elected to play more man coverage and […]
item.content:encoded:
CAN THE LOUISVILLE DEFENSE AVOID A LETDOWN

If you have had the opportunity to read my film reviews this week, you know that your eyes didn’t deceive you when it comes to the defensive performance last weekend. Louisville made a legit change in the defensive scheme when they elected to play more man coverage and added more defenders to the box against the run. They also mugged up their linebackers to cause confusion for the FSU offensive line, and the changes worked.

The key for this week will be to continue to be aggressive up front to create negative plays. Malachi Nelson will be starting for the Orange, and he has not been a consistent passer in his career. Allowing him to have a comfortable experience in the pocket is not a good idea. The Cards have to force him to make quick decisions or to move his feet in the pocket. He does not win in those situations.

VERTICAL PASSING COULD DICTATE THIS GAME

Louisville has the most explosive offense in the country, while the Orange have done well to keep a lid on things as a defense. Syracuse has big outside receivers who have been able to make plays down the field, and we all know how the Cards have struggled to stop big passing plays this season.

We will be in for a very interesting battle of teams who will be looking to push the ball down the field. The Cards showed last weekend that they can prevent explosive passing plays, but the Orange will undoubtedly test the defense to see if it was a fluke.

The Cards haven’t faced a defense that is as good at preventing big passing plays as Syracuse. Wake Forest is about as close as it gets, and the Deacs shut down the explosive aspect of this offense. Brian Brohm will have an opportunity to develop a game plan that will utilize his receivers to create plays down the field.

LOUISVILLE MUST TAKE ADVANTAGE OF SYRACUSE MISTAKES

Syracuse is the most penalized team in the country. Syracuse is among the worst teams in the country when it comes to interceptions thrown. Syracuse will be starting their third-string quarterback in a must-win game. Syracuse has not been able play with a lead this year. Syracuse has only made 46% of their field goals this year.

Pick an issue from the above list, and Louisville needs to pounce on it. The Cards should be in full desperation mode from the first snap of this game, and the Orange will give them opportunities to take advantage of. Pick one and run with it.

COULD WE SEE TAYON HOLLOWAY TRAVEL WITH UMARI HATCHER

If you are a long-time reader, you know that I have repeatedly hoped that the defensive staff would allow the top cornerback on the team to “shadow” the top receiver on the other team. It’s not something you see at the college level, but there’s no good reason why it can’t happen.

Tayon Holloway showed last week why he is a potential NFL prospect as he broke up multiple passes on slant routes while also taking away options for Austin Daniels on other plays. Holloway has great size, and he plays a physical style of play that works well in man coverage.

Why can’t he travel with Umari Hatcher, who is the obvious top option for the Orange? Hatcher lines up at different positions, but Louisville can play with three cornerbacks if needed, and they can use different coverages. It may be worth expending more effort if it means you can take Hatcher out of the game.

NOTES

  • Syracuse has twin brothers Davien and Davion Kerr on their team. They wear the same number.
  • At one point, Nelson was the overall number one high school prospect in the 2023 class.
  • Louisville had 36 pressures last weekend, with Clev Lubin notching 12 on his own. For context, they had 16 pressures in the Ole Miss game.

item.title: Jets getting much-needed offensive boost with Omar Cooper Jr., Kenyon Sadiq returning
item.description: The Jets offense won’t be whole for at least another week. The unit will be healthier than it was last Sunday, though.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets offense won’t be whole for at least another week. 

The unit will be healthier than it was last Sunday, though. 

Take flight with the Jets

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

tRY IT NOW

Consider that progress. 

While No. 2 receiver Adonai Mitchell, top running back Breece Hall and starting left guard Dylan Parham were ruled out Friday for the Jets’ AFC East opener, rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq are expected to play against the rival Patriots. 

Sadiq suffered a concussion against the Browns last Sunday, but was able to practice fully Friday for the first time this week. Cooper, meanwhile, has been out since Week 1 after injuring his ankle at the tail end of his first NFL reception, a 30-yard catch and run. That duo may be able to ease the burden on star wideout Garrett Wilson, who will have to deal with top cornerback Christian Gonzalez. 

The Jets are going to need more out of their offense. They have managed only 29 points over the past two games, and rank 23rd in passing, 26th in total offense and 27th in points scored. 

Gang Green is facing an offense that has come alive this week. After a shaky start, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has thrown seven touchdown passes the last two weeks, as New England has exploded for 74 points in wins over the Bills and Raiders. Their defense has performed well up to this point as well, fourth in the league in points allowed (18.8). 

One way to combat an explosive offense is to keep them off the field. The good news is Hall’s backup, Braelon Allen, is coming off a career game. In the win over the Browns, he ran for a personal-best 116 yards on 24 carries along with the game-winning, fourth-quarter touchdown. 

“I thought Braelon did a hell of a job, and not just Braelon but the whole O-line and the run concepts that we had,” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said. “And even a couple runs that [Isaiah Davis] got I thought were pretty good. So, coming into this week, knowing that we’re going against a good defense, a tough opponent, it’s going to be critical for us to make sure we establish that run game so we can open up everything else when it comes to the passing game.” 

New England will of course look to make the Jets one-dimensional by shutting down Allen. That’s where Sadiq and Cooper can be so important. The Jets used two of their three first-round picks on the duo, partly to be less dependent on Wilson every Sunday and also to add more weapons to the attack.

Sadiq has enjoyed one big game so far, a seven-catch, 105-yard effort in a Week 3 loss to the Lions. The Jets would like to unlock him and Cooper on Sunday. 

There were high hopes for Cooper, who caught 69 passes for 937 yards and 13 touchdowns for national champion Indiana. After a quiet training camp, the No. 30 overall pick flashed in the opener against the Titans with that long catch in which he made a few defenders miss. 

Unfortunately, the play ended with an injury. But on Sunday, he will be back. 

“Excited to see him back out there and excited about what he can contribute to this offense,” offensive coordinator Frank Reich said.

If you’re looking for David Bailey on social media, you’re not going to find the Jets’ prized rookie edge rusher anywhere. 

Early in the season, Bailey deleted his Instagram account. 

Take flight with the Jets

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

tRY IT NOW

“I feel like, honestly, I spent too much time on Instagram,” the No. 2 overall pick out of Texas Tech said. “So I gave myself a little bit of a break. I don’t really know how long that break is going to go. If I feel the need to download it again, I’ll get it. But for now, I think I’m good. 

“You start scrolling, you got your reels, which are pretty addicting. I felt like I was spending too much time on it. There’s time that I could’ve devoted to other things, like putting more time into my body, studying the playbook or just other productive things I could’ve been doing.” 

Bailey never had an account on X. After his breakout performance Sunday, when he had three sacks and was named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week, he isn’t planning to change anything. 

“It felt good,” he said. “I feel like that game really could’ve happened to anybody, especially on the defensive line. We were all doing really well with our assignments and our jobs. It could’ve come to anybody that day.” 

The Patriots have a number of key players who are listed as questionable. All three players were limited throughout the week of practice. “To me, it wasn’t a dirty hit,” he said. “It was just a football play.”

item.title: New York Jets: Geno Smith Appreciation Post
item.description: Geno has done a nice job in his return to the Jets
item.content:encoded:
As someone who prides himself on objective analysis, it’s equally important for me to acknowledge the highs, no matter how rare they are, in addition to the many lows that come with being a New York Jets fan. I’ll be the first to admit I was very underwhelmed with the Geno Smith acquisition – I understood the huge financial benefit of having a starting-caliber QB under contract for $3.3 million but had no belief in Geno in 2026.

I didn’t even believe in him from 2013-2016. His Seattle Seahawks days were cool, but even his last year there started to look ugly until he went to Vegas and the wheels completely fell off. No QB in the NFL threw more interceptions from 2024-2025 than Eugene Cyril Smith. 15 in 2024 (2nd in the NFL), 17 in 2025 (1st in the NFL), I thought we were in for another brutal showing at quarterback this year. Boy, was I wrong.

Only three quarterbacks this season have started every game this season and thrown zero interceptions: Jared Goff, CJ Stroud, and Geno Smith. After being the most prolific thrower of interceptions for two years, Geno has done a masterful job of avoiding throwing into harm’s way. In fact, he’s become the second passer this century to lead the league in interceptions and then have zero interceptions in his first five games the next year.

I dug deep into ESPN.com to discover that fact – only Vinny Testaverde was able to do this, in 2001, after throwing 25(!) picks in 2000. Still, he got his first interception in Week 6 and ended the 2001 season with 14. Geno has six touchdowns and zero picks after five weeks just like Vinny did, but I’m not sure if this middle-of-the-pack New England defense has what it takes to pick him off. I’m thinking Geno might’ve actually turned over a new leaf.

This isn’t to say he’s been perfect: he’s fumbled in four of the five games so far, and only four players in the league have lost more fumbles than Geno this season. He looks more “gun-shy” than normal this year, which has led him to hold on to the ball longer behind an offensive line that hasn’t lived up to expectations so far.

But I promise this is an appreciationpost, so that’s where my criticism ends! Geno’s avoided interceptions, and he’s put Garrett Wilson on pace for the best season of his career by a large margin. Garrett’s current pace is set for 105 catches, 1,271 yards, and 10 touchdowns this year – all of these numbers would break his previous career bests of 101 catches, 1,104 yards, and 7 touchdowns, which all came in 2024 with Aaron Rodgers slinging the ball.

Smith’s numbers aren’t quite on pace to beat Rodgers, but you could argue his conditions have been less than ideal. We’ve only seen one drive of the Jets offense at full strength with the original trio of Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper Jr. on the field at the same time. We’re still unsure of when that will happen, as Mitchell works his way back from a somewhat mysterious finger injury that required surgery.

Geno has also played 40% of his games in the rain, which is a less-than-ideal condition for pass-happy offenses. The Jets defense gets all the credit for holding opposing pass offenses under 200 yards during these games, but the Jets pass offense has also suffered from the precipitation. What would this offense look like with sunny skies, all the wide receivers healthy, Breece Hall healthy, and the confident Kenyon Sadiq who broke out against the Lions?

It may be a few weeks until we find out, but Geno has done a superb job steadying the ship in the meantime. For me to enter this season as one of his biggest detractors, I cannot stress enough how impressed I am with this start and how hopeful I am for the rest of the season with him at the helm. Now the idea of having him start in 2027 with a young first-round pick QB learning behind him is starting to sound more like a dream than a nightmare. Let’s go, Geno!
